state: CanLang is an AI-authored company SaaS DSL. Adoption, compact source, explicit business policy and one canonical operation path are requirements. Current evidence: Rust compiler is a dependency-free command scaffold; Python is a syntax prototype; VS Code extension is TextMate highlighting, without LSP; 39 Can apps and 21 desired JS files exist, not executable generated programs. Apps target JS directly for workerd; libraries are authored in TS. Generated business modules use @canlang/stdlib and @canlang/ui, shared schemas and canonical invocation. workerd/Web APIs, Wrangler, Cloudflare managed services and maintained libraries can be reused. Five HUMAN-launched Muse coordinators each get one worktree, share it with their own disjoint subagents, and repeatedly open/review/merge small PRs to main. No coordinator creates another orchestrator or nested worktree. Need similar substantial workloads, exclusive paths, early shared interfaces, and a first real integrated app rather than five isolated mock successes. No measured implementation throughput exists. Required domains: parsing/types/composition, IR/codegen, lint/format/LSP/editor, exact values/query/auth/transactions, schedules/outbox/receipts/providers/files, identity/UI/i18n/MCP, assembly/deploy/migrations/local dev/BDD execution/release. D1 mutations use the specified optimistic fence and atomic batch; other writers must join it. Current typed-history and population proposals are not settled. Unresolved semantics must be diagnosed, not invented. Scheme A: lane1 all Rust compilation plus lint/format/LSP/editor; lane2 authoritative state, queries, scalar rules and core stdlib; lane3 durable work, providers and files; lane4 identity, browser UI/i18n and MCP; lane5 assembly, local dev, provisioning/deploy, migration orchestration, inline BDD runner, integration and releases. A keeps Rust analysis ownership unified but lane1 has many toolchain features; lane5 must ship executable integration throughout rather than waiting. Scheme B: lane1 Rust parsing/checking/IR/codegen; lane2 authoring lint/format/LSP/editor and agent diagnostics; lane3 state/core stdlib plus identity; lane4 work/services/files; lane5 browser UI/MCP plus assembly/deployment/local dev/BDD/integration/releases. B isolates authoring work and allows two Rust teams, but requires an early shared analysis API and adds interface/hosting load to lane5. Both reuse one parser/checker, canonical auth and one commit implementation; neither duplicates business rules or exempts tests. Both start with small versioned contracts and provider-owned conformance fixtures, allow contract-only work while a dependency lands, and replace test doubles with genuine integrations before claiming that milestone. Shared root manifests/lockfiles have a single named owner. Compare whole scope, not just number of headings.

partition.instructions: Which partition is the stronger starting assignment for five concurrently productive owners, considering coordination, complete workload and later convergence, without assuming measured speed?

criteria.A: A uses one compiler/tooling owner, one state owner, one async/services/files owner, one identity/UI/MCP owner and one platform/qualification owner.
criteria.B: B separates language engine from authoring tools; state includes identity, async work/files remain together, and UI/MCP shares platform/qualification.
